title: Kahana vs Ko-fi: Library Beside Patronage
excerpt: Ko-fi is recurring membership, patronage, or exclusive fan content. Kahana is library discovery and flexible hub pricing beside patronage.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Ko-fi: popular tipping + membership platform for artists, writers, cosplayers, and indie creators; 0% platform fees on donations/tips for standard users; Ko-fi Gold adds features for ≈USD 6/month.
Buy Me a Coffee: similar scope (tips, memberships, simple digital products) with a flat ≈5% platform fee on all payments.

strengths.title: Easy tipping and micro-support
strengths.detail: Fans can quickly send one-off tips or small recurring support, low friction for fans and creators.

strengths.title: Memberships and digital products
strengths.detail: Both support memberships and digital product sales; Ko-fi also supports physical products and commissions.

strengths.title: Low / no platform fees (Ko-fi)
strengths.detail: Ko-fi charges 0% platform fees on tips, creators mainly pay Stripe/PayPal processing, attractive for smaller audiences.

strengths.title: Simple, creator-friendly UX
strengths.detail: Easy page setup, social links, and accepting support with minimal tech needed.

weaknesses.title: Limited advanced membership features
weaknesses.detail: Simpler memberships than Patreon, fewer community tools, tiered rewards, and analytics.

weaknesses.title: Ko-fi commissions take an extra cut
weaknesses.detail: Commission sales can take an additional platform cut on top of PayPal; some artists prefer direct PayPal for high-value work.

weaknesses.title: Buy Me a Coffee platform fee
weaknesses.detail: ≈5% on all earnings can add up at scale.

weaknesses.title: No live video or advanced engagement
weaknesses.detail: Primarily static support + product pages, no built-in live video, scheduling, or session recording.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Ko-fi is recurring membership, patronage, or exclusive fan content. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Ko-fi puts creators first, full control over how you connect with fans, set prices and terms, and get paid instantly.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Ko-fi side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Ko-fi you can use Memberships and Storefronts as first-class product jobs. Fans already live on that membership surface and prefer tiers, posts, or patronage-native extras.

Using Kahana with Ko-fi

You can use both. Ko-fi keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep patronage-native fans on Ko-fi. Dual-list related work on Kahana so people who browse libraries can find it, join a Club, and pay there too without rebuilding your whole fan stack.
